NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 876 4557 8358, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 876 4557 8358, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 13, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:03 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by the Peninsula High School Academic Decathlon team including Associate Principal
Katie Clovis, Academic Advisor and Coach Anne-Marie Voegtlin, and members Keaton
Ramsay, Skylar Lo, Alexandria Lam and Brandon Zhang.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6A-E AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER & OCTOBER 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63217 THROUGH 63266 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $375,859.07 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100120 THROUGH
  100220 IN THE AMOUNT OF $79,640.66 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $455,499.73 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 21, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 13, 2020
 D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 22, 2020

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 5, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  APPROVAL OF THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION INDEMNITY AGREEMENT

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZUCKERMAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION INDEMNITY AGREEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  2020 PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (PMS) REPORT UPDATE PREPARED
  BY WILLDAN ENGINEERING

Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Fred Wickman, Principal Project Manager of Willdan Engineering provided a presentation of
the FY 2020 Pavement Management System Report.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL brought up the City’s current General Plan Update, and
inquired how it may affect certain paving locations, and suggested the possibility of postponing
paving on Silver Spur Road and Deep Valley Drive in the Commercial District until after the
General Plan is finalized. Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba
responded with a suggested project timeline.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN echoed COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL’S comments,
expressing concern about paving next year on Deep Valley Drive due to upcoming projects.

MAYOR SCHMITZ summarized that this report is for the City Council to receive and file, and
that staff would return with a recommended paving schedule for further Council discussion.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN asked for clarification on the 2025 projections, and how they
relate to the budget. Discussion ensued regarding the projected Pavement Condition Index
(PCI) and the unfunded dollar amounts of the projects.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 13, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE 2020 PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (PMS)
  REPORT, INCLUDING THE TECHNICAL MEMO/BUDGET REPORT

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

C.  CARES ACT SMALL BUSINESS / NON-PROFIT ASSISTANCE GRANT PROPOSAL

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the City will receive all CARES Act funding before
processing any reimbursements, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL. COUNCIL
MEMBER MITCHELL confirmed that independent contractors would be excluded, and that
funds cannot be used toward revenue loss.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired if personnel support would qualify in order for companies
to keep personnel on the payroll. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that staff would look
into the parameters allowed for by the State.

Assistant City Manager Davis and City Attorney Davis both explained that staff would explore
the possibility of including HOAs in the list of eligible organizations, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

MAYOR SCHMITZ commended staff for being innovative in finding ways to help the
community.

Public comment was received from Eileen Hupp, President & CEO of the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce, who spoke in support of the proposed grant program.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTION GIVEN TO STAFF TO CREATE A CARES ACT SMALL
  BUSINESS / NON-PROFIT ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAM AND TO
  RETURN TO THE CITY COUNCIL ON OCTOBER 27, 2020 WITH DETAILS
  OF THE PROGRAM FOR CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
reporting that the number of daily new coronavirus cases remains steady. The County is
currently in Tier 1 of the State’s four-tier reopening plan, and has met the State’s metric
threshold to move to Tier 2 but not yet for two consecutive weeks as required. Nail Salons,
wineries, breweries and playgrounds have all been allowed to reopen.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided the following updates regarding upcoming City Events:
  • October 30 will be the second drive-in movie night featuring “The Nightmare Before
  Christmas.” The event is sold out, but staff is looking into opportunities to safely allow
  more spaces.
  • On October 19, registration will open for a Holiday House Decorating Contest that will
  take place in December.
  • The Mayor’s Breakfast Ride will take place in November, involving a trail riding
  experience that highlights certain equestrian points of interest within the City and a video
  featuring the Mayor at each location.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 13, 2020
   •  The drive-through Parade of Lights will be held on December 5 at Ernie Howlett Park
  involving a collection of lit up light displays.
  •  December 19 will be the third drive-in movie night, movie is still to be determined.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported on the League of California Cities’ virtual Annual
Conference and General Assembly that took place last week. She also participated in a
panel discussing climate change and the role of local government.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Government
(SBCCOG) Steering Committee meeting took place last Thursday. She also reported that
the SBCCOG Board meeting will take place October 22.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on the League of California Cities’ virtual Annual Conference,
and commended COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL on her participation on the climate change
panel. She also attended the Los Angeles Division meeting of the conference, where voting
and elections were discussed.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF mentioned the Metropolitan Water District’s announcement to
delay the pipeline re-lining project on Palos Verdes Drive East and the impact on plans for
“Butcher Park.” City Manager Grammer explained that the Park and Activities Commission will
be discussing the proposed improvements to the park this month, and the Commission’s
recommendation would be presented to the City Council at its next meeting.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN inquired about coordinating the paving of Silver Spur Road
in the Commercial District with the City of Rancho Palos Verdes. City Manager Grammer stated
that staff will be reaching out to RPV to see about possibly collaborating on a joint paving
project.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN announced that Target will be opening officially on October
25.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported that the next monthly meeting of the Peninsula City Mayors will
include a discussion with Southern California Edison.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Initiation of litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:45 P.M. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Jerome
(Jerry) Gliksman. The meeting was adjourned to the next regular City Council meeting on
Tuesday, October 27, 2020 at 7:00 P.M. for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 13, 2020
